page.text:
A ring is *commutative* when its multiplication satisfies $a * b = b * a$
for all elements. Commutative rings serve as the algebraic foundation of
algebraic geometry, where geometric shapes (varieties and schemes) are
studied through their commutative rings of polynomial or regular
functions.

In contrast, non-commutative rings—such as matrix rings $M_n(R)$,
endomorphism rings $\operatorname{End}(V)$, and differential
operators—arise naturally as transformation algebras across linear
algebra and quantum physics.
